transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I don’t care about the projects and hobbies I used to love anymore; nothing feels interesting to me now. It's like I've just completely lost my spark, and I can't seem to find the motivation to do any of the things that used to bring me joy.

Have you had other separate periods like this in the past where you felt depressed or lost interest for weeks or months and then got back to your usual self in between? Or has this low mood and loss of interest been present most of the time for at least two years without really letting up?

No, I've never felt like this before—this is the first time I've ever experienced anything like this. It hasn't been two years, but it has been going on for a little over a year now, starting right after I lost a big solar contract and the money got really tight.

During this depression, have you ever heard or seen things that other people couldn’t, or strongly believed something that others said wasn’t true? This includes voices, visions, or fixed beliefs like being ruined or guilty in a way that felt absolutely certain.
No, I've never experienced anything like that. I haven't heard or seen things that other people couldn't, and I don't have any of those kinds of visions or beliefs.

How much has this depression affected your ability to function day to day—for example, are you still able to work, take care of yourself, and manage basic responsibilities, or has that become very difficult or impossible?

It’s severely affected my daily life—I’ve started missing bid deadlines, turning in repair reports late, and canceling on my friends constantly. Because of all this, my income has dropped, and I usually just go straight home after work to sit alone. I've just been letting my chores and bills pile up around me because I can't find the energy to handle them.
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself or ending your life? If yes, have you made any plans or taken any steps toward it?

On the really bad nights, when I'm staring at all those overdue bills, I do catch myself thinking it would be easier if I just didn't wake up tomorrow. I've even pictured crashing my truck on the highway sometimes, but I haven't made any plans or taken any steps to actually do anything.

Have you ever had a period lasting several days or more when you felt unusually energized or euphoric, needed much less sleep, talked faster than usual, or did risky things that were out of character? Even if it happened at a different time than this depression.
No, I've never experienced anything like that. I've only ever felt really down, exhausted, and completely overwhelmed. I definitely haven't had periods of high energy or done anything risky.

During this depression, how have your sleep and appetite changed—are you sleeping much more or less than usual, and have you noticed weight loss or gain? Also, has your energy or ability to concentrate been affected?

I'm sleeping much less, lying awake worrying about bills and waking up at 3 or 4 AM unable to drift back off. My appetite is gone too; I have to force myself to eat because everything tastes like cardboard. On top of that, my concentration is shot—I have to reread simple emails multiple times and get completely frozen by basic decisions.

final_diagnosis.reason: First depressive episode with persistent depressed mood/anhedonia, insomnia, reduced appetite, impaired concentration/indecisiveness, low energy, marked functional impairment, and suicidal ideation. No history of manic/hypomanic episodes and no psychotic symptoms. Duration is over a year, but the presentation began after a major financial stressor and is described as a first episode rather than chronic longstanding dysthymia.
